title: Immunohistochemical detection of preproenkephalin in the mouse brain
protocol: Anesthetize the mouse by intraperitoneal injection of sodium pentobarbital according to manufacturer guidelines.
Immobolize the fully anesthetized animal on an appropriate surface surrounded by a plastic container for recovery of any biological fluid.
Cut open the chest and secure the tissue to obtain visibility of the heart.
Insert a 20-gauge needle hooked up to a perfusion pump into the left ventricle.
Perform a small incision into the left atrium and perfuse the animal at 3ml/min with TBS for 3 minutes.
Switch the perfusion to CS at 3ml/min for an additional 3 minutes.
Remove the brain from the skull and postfix it in CS for 1 hour at room temperature.
Wash the tissue twice with TBS to remove residual CS and place it in CPB until it sinks to the bottom of the tube.
Wash the brain twice with TBS to remove excess sucrose.
Embed the brain in OCT and snap-freeze it using liquid nitrogen. Store blocks at -80°C until use.
Prepare cryosections of 30-to-40 µm thickness in the appropriate orientation using a cryostat. Place free-floating sections in 24 well plates with 300µl TBS maintaining the sequential order.
Wash the sections twice with 300µl TBS for 10 minutes.
Incubate for 30 minutes at room temperature with QS.
Wash three times with 300 µl WS.
Incubate for 1 hour at room temperature with BB.
Remove BB and incubate tissues with 200µl AIB containing a 1:200 dilution of anti-preproenkephalin antibody. Incubate overnight at 4°C with gentle rocking.
Wash tissues three times as above.
Incubate with Alexa488-conjugated secondary antibody diluted 1:1000 in AIB for 3 hours at room temperature with gentle rocking.
Wash tissues three times as above.
Counterstain the tissue with 100 ng/ml DAPI for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Wash tissues once as above.
Place sections on a gelatin-coated slide using a fine brush.
Mount the slides using Vectashield Mounting Medium and cover with a coverslip glass.
Seal the edges of the coverslip with nail polish to reduce oxidation of the mounting medium.
Let the slides dry at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Proceed with the analysis.
